gloss_en: evil thoughts (machashavot ra'ot) — morally bad or impure thoughts arising in a person's mind, likened in Likutey Moharan I:233 to impure (non-kosher) animals set to battle against holy thoughts

outliers.actual_gloss_en: alien/foreign thoughts — distracting extraneous thoughts, specifically those that intrude during prayer, likened to clouds covering the eyes
outliers.reason: The text reads מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת (alien thoughts), a distinct phrase and distinct concept in LM I:2 (thoughts intruding in prayer due to corrupted judgment), not מחשבות רעות; the surface form does not even match the canonical Hebrew.

gloss_en: ishah — woman/wife as the feminine archetype (e.g., Chavah, Esther, the Shekhinah); in Rabbi Nachman's typology the receptive female partner paired with 'ish', standing for faith, fear, the Holy Tongue, or livelihood

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the word ishah does not occur in this proof or paragraph; the passage concerns the 'path in the sea' (derekh) and the Elul kavanot
outliers.reason: mis-assignment — the form אשה is absent from both the proof text and the surrounding paragraph, so no sense of 'woman' can be attested here

gloss_en: Adam / man — the archetypal human being (אָדָם), the pinnacle of creation identified with Torah ("zot ha-Torah adam"), speech, Israel, and the Divine name Havayah spelled with alfin (gematria 45 = מ"ה); the status one attains through tzedakah and fasting ("na'aseh adam"), and the first man paired with Chava. Not the color-word אָדֹם ('red'), the nation אֱדוֹם, or the participle מְדַבֵּר ('speaker').

outliers.actual_gloss_en: one who speaks (medaber) — the 'speech of tzedakah' from Isaiah 63
outliers.reason: The form אדם never appears in this proof; the passage concerns רִבּוּעַ הַדִּבּוּר and the verse 'מְדַבֵּר בִּצְדָקָה'. The occurrence is really about דיבור/מְדַבֵּר, a different word mis-assigned to אָדָם.

gloss_en: the evil spirit (ruach ra'ah) — the melancholic spirit of folly and sadness identified with the imaginative faculty, which opposes and confuses the good spirit of prophecy (as with Shaul in I Samuel 16)

outliers.actual_gloss_en: a bad wind — hatred as a turbulent wind/disturbance of the air that prevents speech from being heard (Judges 9:23)
outliers.reason: In lm1:17 ruach is used in its 'wind' sense (bilbul ha-avir, contrasted with still pure air), not the psychological evil spirit of melancholy/imagination in lm1:54

gloss_en: sleep (שֵׁנָה) — the state of slumber in which the mind/soul rests and is renewed; used by Rabbi Nachman both literally (bodily sleep induced by the cold-moist lungs) and expansively (constricted consciousness, simple Torah study, faith-based commerce as modes of 'sleep')

outliers.actual_gloss_en: year (unit of time)
outliers.reason: Proof concerns Yitzchak alluding to זְמַן/time via 'מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם' (end of two YEARS); the form here is שָׁנָה 'year', a homograph of שֵׁנָה 'sleep', and the partner זמן confirms the temporal sense.

gloss_en: Arrogance (gadlut) — haughty self-aggrandizement, the negative character trait of pride identified in Likutey Moharan 11 with idolatry (the 'seven houses of idol worship') and arising from the fall of the divine garment of splendor (tiferet); NOT the positive 'greatness/expanded consciousness' (gadlut ha-mochin)

outliers.actual_gloss_en: Greatness / expanded spiritual state (gadlut, as opposed to katnut) — the elevated, empowered condition into which Rabbi Shimon brings Rabbi Akiva so that he is compelled to reveal Torah
outliers.reason: Same letters but opposite valence: here gadlut is a desirable expanded state overcoming humility-driven reticence, contrasted with the arrogance-as-idolatry sense of lm1:11; a distinct sense, not an inflectional variant.

gloss_en: Abraham (Avraham) the biblical patriarch, who in Likutey Moharan embodies chesed (lovingkindness), love (ahavah), faith, and the 'right side' — the archetype of the attribute of loving devotion

outliers.actual_gloss_en: limbs/organs (of the body), as in the 248 limbs corresponding to the 248 positive commandments
outliers.reason: Proof at lm2:26 is entirely about Moshe being clothed in each of Israel's 248 limbs; Abraham is not the subject. The partner רמ"ח איברים indicates the matched word is really אֵבָרִים (limbs), a different word sharing letters — a homograph/mis-assignment.

gloss_en: mas (מַס) — tribute / compulsory labor-service, as in Jacob's blessing 'va-yehi le-mas oved' (Gen 49:15), the tribute-bearing servant; homiletically linked by sound to מסמוס (dissolving/melting away)

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the letter-pair mem and samekh of the Tablets (which stood by miracle, Shabbat 104a), expounded as the aspect of forgetfulness
outliers.reason: Here מַס is not the word 'tribute' but the combination of the letters mem+samekh from the Talmudic dictum about the Tablets; a homograph of the biblical מַס of Gen 49:15.

gloss_en: water (Heb. מַיִם / Aram. מַיָּא) — the liquid element as a symbolic bechina in Likutey Moharan: the heart poured out before God ('pour out your heart like water'), charity/tzedakah, and the male and female waters (mayin dukhrin u-nukvin) from which man is formed; the physical noun 'water' itself, not any other word sharing these letters

outliers.actual_gloss_en: water (as symbol of Torah) — but the form does not appear in the cited evidence
outliers.reason: The proof and paragraph (lm2:32 on sefer = Name of God, migdal oz shem H') contain no occurrence of מים at all; the water=Torah link is not attested in the shown text, so this is a probable mis-assignment of proof/occurrence.

gloss_en: the hand (yad) — the bodily hand as a mystical symbol and active organ: the hand of clapping, music, and joy ('you shall rejoice in all the undertakings of your hand'), of prophecy ('by the hand of the prophets I was imaged'), of judgment/the square ('My hand takes hold of judgment'), and embodying the Name Havayah (yud = 10, dalet = 4); NOT the grammaticalized idiom עַל־יַד / עַל־יָדָם ('by means of, through the agency of')

outliers.actual_gloss_en: through them / by their agency (instrumental idiom)
outliers.reason: The proof and paragraph contain יד only inside the idiomatic phrase 'שֶׁעַל יָדָם' ('through whom'), a grammaticalized preposition of agency; the conceptual hand (הַיָּד) claimed by the vocalization does not appear in the cited text, so this looks like a mis-assignment.

gloss_en: Scent, fragrance (רֵיחַ) — an odor perceived through the nose/nostrils, the spiritual sense of smell linked to purity and awe of Heaven (as in 'תְּהִלָּתִי אֶחֱטָם לָךְ' and 'וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה''); distinct from the homographs/near-forms רֵאָה 'lung' and רוּחַ 'wind, spirit'

outliers.actual_gloss_en: lung (the bodily organ, whose wings fan the heart; 'named re'ah because it illuminates the eyes')
outliers.reason: The proof and paragraph speak exclusively of הָרֵאָה (the lung), its wings and wind, and the Chullin 49a derasha on the lung illuminating the eyes; no form of רֵיחַ 'scent' appears. This is a different word sharing similar letters, not the scent sense.

gloss_en: earth / land (אֶרֶץ, the physical ground or terrestrial realm; incl. Aramaic cognate אַרְעָא) — used homiletically as a base 'bechina' term that Rabbi Nachman identifies via prooftexts with fear ('eretz yar'ah'), the soul ('nafshi ke-eretz'), faith ('shekhan eretz u-re'eh emunah'), and the body (earth vs. heaven = body vs. soul)

outliers.actual_gloss_en: unverifiable — the word ארץ does not appear in the cited proof or paragraph
outliers.reason: The proof/paragraph from lm2:82 (about chokhmah, mah, Adam, vitality) contains no occurrence of ארץ, and the claimed bechina link to חוה (Eve) cannot be confirmed from the shown text; likely a mis-assignment.

gloss_en: potential (koach) — the latent, not-yet-actualized state of a thing, paired with and opposed to po'al (the actual/actualized), as in bringing something 'from potential to actual'; the initial thought before the deed

outliers.actual_gloss_en: strength, force — the power/vigor exerted (here, praying with strength, 'He gives you strength to make wealth')
outliers.reason: Same spelling and vocalization, but here כח means exerted strength/power (praying with koach to rectify Malkhut), not the philosophical 'potential' opposed to 'actual' of lm1:66; distinct sense.

gloss_en: the firstborn (bekhor) — the firstborn son himself, identified as the aspect of the intellect/reishit (as in Yaakov, the 'firstborn' who embodies chokhmah)

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the birthright — the right/status of primogeniture (which Yaakov acquired), not the firstborn person
outliers.reason: Distinct lexeme בְּכוֹרָה (abstract feminine 'birthright', with final ה) rather than בְּכוֹר 'firstborn'; 'זָכָה לַבְּכוֹרָה' means he merited the birthright-status.

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the birthright — the firstborn's double portion (pi shnayim) which Yosef received, identified with the service of prayer
outliers.reason: Again בְּכוֹרָה 'birthright' (נָטַל אֶת הַבְּכוֹרָה), a different word from בְּכוֹר 'firstborn person'; refers to the inherited status/portion, not a firstborn.

gloss_en: the rainbow (keshet) — the arc seen in the clouds as the sign of God's covenant after the Flood, symbolizing the tzaddik whose merit protects the generation (Ketubot 77b; 'I will see it to remember the eternal covenant')

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the archer's bow — a weapon that shoots arrows, symbolizing the rectified covenant (tikkun ha-brit) from which the 'arrows' of prayer are shot forth
outliers.reason: Same consonants and vocalization, but a distinct sense: here keshet is the weapon that launches arrows (prayer), not the rainbow of the covenant sign seen in the sky.

gloss_en: Raglin/raglayim — the feet/legs, the lowest limbs of the body (Aramaic raglin), used as a homiletic bechina for the lowest levels: speech, livelihood/money, the rebukers of the generation, the wife/nukva, standing in Torah and prayer, dancing, and the sefirot Netzach-and-Hod

outliers.actual_gloss_en: Regalim — the pilgrimage festivals (regel = appointed time/occasion, as in שלוש רגלים), identified with 'binah la-itim' (understanding of times)
outliers.reason: Vocalized רְגָלִים and equated with בינה לעתים (times/festivals), i.e. regel in the sense of 'occasion/festival' (cf. Num 22:28 'שלוש רגלים'), not the body-limb sense raglayim/raglin carried by all other occurrences

gloss_en: the Sage of the Generation (chakham ha-dor) — the singular leading Torah sage/true tzaddik of his generation, the 'comprehensive mind' (moach ha-kolel) from whom all individual minds of the generation receive their illumination

outliers.actual_gloss_en: the wise man / sage in general — one who is likened to the ant (Proverbs 6) and teaches knowledge and God's ways to the people
outliers.reason: Form is only הֶחָכָם, not חכם הדור; context is the generic wise man of the Proverbs verse compared to an ant, not the specific title 'sage of the generation' as the comprehensive mind. Likely mis-assignment to this narrower titled concept.

gloss_en: Love (ahavah) — the spiritual quality/emotion of love: the attribute (middah) of Abraham corresponding to Chesed, the attachment of spirit to spirit (love of God and between souls), including 'holy loves' (ahavot di-kedushah); the noun אַהֲבָה, not any other word

outliers.actual_gloss_en: after the decree has been issued (a temporal phrase about prayer after a heavenly verdict)
outliers.reason: The vocalized text and proof contain no form of אהבה at all; the occurrence is about clothing prayer after a gzar din — a plain mis-assignment to this concept.

gloss_en: Ge'ulah — the Redemption: the national-messianic deliverance of Israel from exile, brought about through repentance and faith (as in 'in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed')

outliers.actual_gloss_en: exile (Aramaic galuta, 'they will go out from the exile through it')
outliers.reason: The word גאולה does not actually appear here; the vocalized form is the Aramaic גָּלוּתָא (exile) in the Zohar phrase יִפְקוּן בֵּהּ מִן גָּלוּתָא. Redemption is only implied by negation of exile — a different lexeme, so a form-level mis-assignment.

gloss_en: The act of breaking/subduing (shevirah) the lust for adultery — the deliberate conquest performed upon the sexual lust, which serves as a means (e.g., for rectifying the mochin/mind); distinct from the lust of adultery itself

outliers.actual_gloss_en: The lust for adultery itself (the bonfire of the seventy stars), which is nullified by the speech of the Holy Tongue
outliers.reason: The text reads 'בְּחִינַת תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף שֶׁנִּתְבַּטֵּל' — it names the lust itself (as object nullified by holy speech); the noun of action שְׁבִירַת does not appear, so this occurrence is the lust, not the act of breaking it.

gloss_en: Ibbur — 'gestation/pregnancy': the embryonic state in which the mochin (divine intellect/influx) are concealed and constricted as in a womb, prior to their 'birth' (leidah); associated with judgment and with Yaakov ('in the womb he grasped the heel')

outliers.actual_gloss_en: grain, produce (Aramaic ibbura, as in the Talmudic phrase 'buy grain for a zuz')
outliers.reason: In Ta'anit 23b עִבּוּרָא means grain to purchase; R. Nachman expounds it only via gematria (ע"ב + רי"ו), not as gestation. Homograph of the gestation sense.
